sections.title: Current evidence resolves the earlier narrow concerns
sections.text:
As of 2026-10-26T00:42:21.519Z, the supplied evidence supports the manuscript's restricted scientific chain without an identified sign, normalization, derivative-order, or pressure-convention mismatch. The six source-judgment targets are answered here using existing checks and source assessments; this does not rewrite the deterministic plan or create new checker results. The Schwarzschild decomposition target is interpretive rather than an additional theorem.

The current reconciliation repairs the old missing link for \(F_L=U/L\). Its two remaining canonical entries exceed complete scalar representation, but the restricted derivation supplies additional conditional support. They should not be counted as two unresolved mathematical failures. Likewise, obsolete statements that references were unread, companions unavailable, or checks merely proposed no longer describe the current record.

The supporting companion is separate from the one-page submission, and the referenced full manuscript has not been assumed. The accepted-correction overlay is empty. No actual manuscript source uncertainty is recorded. The literature record's identified abstract/title mismatch for 2201.12141 is a retrieval-quality caution about that external record; it is not evidence against this manuscript and is not used decisively here.

Explicit premises remain essential: the EH theory and orientation, selected boundary polarization, physical clock/generator, null-preserving tangent variations, controlled shear/generator/matter and corner responses, and the fixed-domain stationary reduction. No missing scientific premise is identified for the narrow claim under these supplied conditions. Arbitrary-gauge covariance, moving-cut/global-corner certification, and existence of arbitrary on-shell source families remain uncomputed extensions, not accomplishments of this review and not prerequisites imposed on a claim that disclaims them. There are no open material issues in this assessment; historical priority is the remaining open clarification.

priorWorkSection.title: The supported advance is the length-work identification
priorWorkSection.text:
The closest prior result is the action response, not merely \(TS\). Parattu et al., Equations (111)–(113), derives the area-weighted surface-gravity variation from gravitational momentum variation in its specified static horizon setting. Hopfmüller–Freidel develops the null scalar conjugacy, exact-variation exchange, and corner structure. Odak et al. compares different scalar polarizations explicitly. Those results are foundations, not discoveries of this manuscript.

The membrane comparison is nevertheless not an identity of all pressures. Kolekar–Kothawala's examined passages derive a tangential surface stress and connect its area product to heat content. The manuscript's \(P_L=\Pi/L\) has different dimensions and is the coefficient of a different scale variation. Wang's evolving FLRW membrane construction includes generator/regulator-dependent pressure corrections; it is not the same object as the present instantaneous scalar screen pressure. These additional membrane and phase-space works were discovered during review and must not be attributed to the author's one-page bibliography.

The supplied claim-specific novelty findings therefore support a partly distinctive mechanical interpretation and a distinct FRW screen assignment, with moderate confidence. The search audit includes focused queries and bounded citation neighborhoods, with earlier failed seed lookups subsequently resolved. It is not an exhaustive priority search. An earlier full-text construction using the same length source, action response, and normal-pressure interpretation would change the novelty finding. Conversely, a useful identification need not introduce new dynamics or an experiment to contribute to the field's explanation.
